title: Sell Mineral Rights in Huntley, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Huntley, MT
metaDescription: Huntley gave its name to the Yellowstone Valley's namesake irrigation project. A retired engineer explains what that reclamation-era history means for title.
heroLead: The Huntley Project takes its name from this town, and that reclamation-era irrigation history is still visible in how mineral title reads on deeds here.
intro: Huntley sits at the heart of the irrigation district that bears its name, one of the early Bureau of Reclamation projects along the Yellowstone River developed in the first decade of the twentieth century. Land here was parceled out to homesteaders under reclamation-era rules, and mineral severance, where it exists, generally happened later as farms sold or passed through generations.

sections.heading: Reclamation-Era Title Quirks
paragraphs: Some reclamation-project deeds carry water-right language alongside mineral provisions, which can make the original patent documents more layered to read than a standard homestead deed elsewhere in the state. If your family's interest near Huntley goes back to the original project era, I'd want to see the actual patent and any subsequent severance deed before confirming exactly what you hold.

sections.heading: Development Reality Around Huntley
paragraphs: This remains productive irrigated agricultural ground, not an active oil and gas area. I check current permitting for Yellowstone County broadly, but tracts around Huntley specifically have historically seen little to no drilling interest, and I set that expectation honestly from the start.

sections.heading: What a Fair Look Involves
paragraphs: I'd confirm the recorded chain of title, check whether the interest has ever been leased, and give a value range reflecting the area's quiet development history. For most owners here, that's a modest, speculative figure tied to long-term potential rather than any current royalty stream.

I also ask whether the family still has the original reclamation contract from the Bureau of Reclamation, since those documents sometimes describe the mineral reservation in more detail than the deed that eventually got recorded at the courthouse decades later.

faqs.question: Why does my family's deed near Huntley mention water rights alongside minerals?
faqs.answer: Huntley sits within an early Bureau of Reclamation irrigation project, and some original patents from that era bundle water-right language with the mineral provisions. It's worth reading the full original patent to understand exactly what was reserved.

faqs.question: Is there oil and gas activity near Huntley, MT?
faqs.answer: Little to none historically. This is productive irrigated farmland rather than an area with meaningful drilling history.

faqs.question: Where do I find the original land patent for property near Huntley?
faqs.answer: The Yellowstone County Clerk and Recorder in Billings holds the recorded chain of title, and the Bureau of Land Management's General Land Office records can often show the original federal patent as well.

faqs.question: Should I request records directly from the Bureau of Reclamation?
faqs.answer: It's worth a try if the courthouse chain of title is unclear on mineral severance. Original project-era contracts sometimes spell out reservations in more detail than what eventually got summarized into a later recorded deed.
